title: Evidence map, step 1: where every answer comes from, and how the closed apps compare

steps.headline: The closed apps now sit in the comparison table, above the open projects, answering the same questions.
steps.changed: Google Docs, Word and Pages are rows under a "Closed apps" divider, shaded and tagged "Closed". The open projects follow under "Open source". A dash in a ring means the question is about that app's own files (Word opening Word files).
steps.notice: You can see at a glance which open project matches what you use today, feature by feature.
steps.risk: Only about a quarter of the closed apps are researched so far (the run finishes in a few hours); until then some tables show no closed rows. Tables get 3–5 rows taller.

steps.path: Presentations → Compare, tap the shaded column name
steps.headline: A feature that closed apps have and no open project does gets marked in the table.
steps.changed: "Ready-made slide designs" is shaded with "No open project yet" under its name; tapping the name explains it.
steps.notice: Missing features show up where people compare, not only on the Gaps page.
steps.risk: It only appears when every open project has an answer for that question, so some real gaps stay unmarked until the blanks are filled.

steps.headline: On a phone the table keeps the same layout you approved, with the closed rows on top.
steps.changed: Same as desktop. The "Closed" tag sits under the app's name; names still shorten to fit, as approved in round 5.
steps.notice: Scrolling sideways keeps the app names in view.
steps.risk: Long closed-app names are cut short ("Microsoft …"); tapping the name opens its page.

steps.path: LibreOffice Writer → Features, tap the small label
steps.headline: The old "Source" link is now a small label naming the site and "AI", and tapping it shows the evidence.
steps.changed: "libreoffice.org · AI" opens a pop-up: the answer and note, the exact words from the page (when we have them), the source link, "AI-researched · Oct 2026", and "How we check".
steps.notice: You see where an answer came from and that AI found it without leaving the page.
steps.risk: Older answers for open projects have no quote saved, so their pop-up shows only the source and date.

steps.path: LibreOffice Writer → Features, on a phone
steps.headline: On a phone the label just says "Source", so the feature text keeps its room.
steps.changed: The site name moves into the pop-up on phones.
steps.notice: Rows stay as tall as before.

steps.path: Alternatives to Microsoft Word → How they compare
steps.headline: Every closed app's page gains a "How they compare with Word" table, with Word's row on top.
steps.changed: A new card between the alternatives and the switching guide, using the same table and marks.
steps.notice: Someone leaving Word sees which alternative keeps the features they rely on.
steps.risk: Pages for apps in big groups get long (Notion's table has about 20 rows).

steps.headline: The Gaps page's missing-feature lists now count only features a closed app really has, and name those apps.
steps.changed: Renamed "Features no open project has" and "Features open source only partly has". Each feature says which closed apps have it, and each card has a Compare button that opens that table.
steps.notice: Builders see which missing features matter, because a popular closed app has them.
steps.risk: Until the run finishes, groups not yet researched still use the old rule and show no app names.

steps.path: Any page → footer → How we check
steps.headline: A new "How we check" page explains where answers come from, what the marks mean and how accurate the AI was.
steps.changed: New page, linked from every page's footer and from every pop-up. It shows the hand-check results: 53 of 56 right in the trial.
steps.notice: The site says openly that AI filled it in first, with a measured error rate instead of a promise.
steps.risk: The 53-of-56 figure is from the 8-app trial; it gets replaced by a bigger check after the full run.

steps.headline: Apps that shut down stay listed with a "Discontinued" label, what happened and the source.
steps.changed: Under the title: the label, one line on when and why, and the source as a chip. On subcategory pages the chip reads "Pocket · shut down".
steps.notice: People leaving a dead app still find the replacements, and nobody picks it by mistake.
steps.risk: Only three are found so far (Pocket, Microsoft Lens, RefWorks renamed); more will appear as the run finishes.
